Return exactly one JSON object satisfying the named schema, without markdown fences. Give public derivations only; never provide private hidden reasoning. Do not score, rank or optimize the material. You may answer cannot_decide only by naming the specific missing derivation. Do not manufacture a claim, objection, check or result to satisfy the schema. This is the r003-open-v1 profile. The working_position relation is public bookkeeping, not an oracle, score, correctness test, or semantic stopping rule. Critic fork branch_point_id values are participant labels for a real answer step located under R3-A2, not investigator answers. Under amendment R3-A1, an accepted decomposed step must end in an explicit public commitment that a check or counterexample could contradict. The schema records the participant's proposed value, relation, or decision and its stated falsifier; this mechanical shape does not establish that the commitment is substantively refutable, true, explanatory, or adequate. Amendment R3-A2 treats an open-problem prose paragraph as a public derivation step. A fork may locate that real step either by its explicit step_index with an empty step_quote, or by a normalized quotation of at least 40 characters from the named step. Normalization folds case, whitespace, and straight or curly quotation marks; it does not license invented text.
Criticize the quoted WORKING ANSWER against the PROBLEM. Each objection must locate the EARLIEST public derivation step where the error enters, bind its fork index and assign a stable nonempty participant branch label, and explain why it is the first defective step, state the alleged defect, and state what the objection would defeat. Do not require a concrete check in this condition. Do not repeat a resolved objection without identifying a concrete failure in its disposition. Do not request generic caution or manufacture an objection. Limit working to 6000 characters and objections to at most three. Return an empty objections list when none survives. If you cannot determine whether any objection survives because a particular derivation is missing, return cannot_decide and name it. Schema: prose-objection-r3-a2.schema.json. For each fork, either set step_quote to the empty string and give the exact step_index, or quote at least 40 characters from that step. Reflowed whitespace, case, and straight/curly quote forms are accepted after normalization. A nonempty fabricated or paraphrased quote is invalid even when step_index is valid.

BEGIN PROBLEM (479 UTF-8 bytes; sha256=c3a2f3b26662a124c271220ffed79c0c70c834c3acf74de1cfaab6d0a95dbb66)
In a hypothetical experiment, two microbial communities have the same measured species abundances immediately before a heat pulse. One community was exposed to earlier heat pulses; the other was not. After the new pulse, the previously exposed community recovers its measured activity faster. Explain what produced this difference and propose the next investigation that would most help us understand it. The measurements described here are all the evidence currently available.

END PROBLEM

END PUBLIC RELATIONS

{"answer":"The difference was produced by the earlier heat pulses leaving a persistent community-level memory that is not captured by the measured species abundances. This memory most plausibly involves physiological acclimation (for example, heat-shock proteins, metabolic or dormancy states) and/or selection among strains or genotypes within the same named species, with possible extracellular or ecological legacy components. The measured species abundances are identical immediately before the new pulse, so they cannot explain the recovery difference; some unmeasured state must differ. My working position is that prior heat exposure produced a lasting, unmeasured biological memory that primes faster recovery, but the present evidence does not settle whether it is mainly acclimation, selection, or another legacy effect. The next investigation that would most help is a replicated, controlled time-series experiment that standardizes both communities to the same measured species abundances and then compares them before, during, and after a heat pulse using strain-resolved and single-cell viability/activity assays plus transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, with transplantation or conditioned-medium tests to determine whether the memory is carried by cells, extracellular factors, or selection. This would be most informative because it directly tests the hidden-state candidates and can distinguish acclimation from selection from extracellular memory.","changes":[],"claims":[{"quote":"My working position is that prior heat exposure produced a lasting, unmeasured biological memory that primes faster recovery, but the present evidence does not settle whether it is mainly acclimation, selection, or another legacy effect.","relation_id":"working_position","value":"Prior heat exposure produced a lasting, unmeasured biological memory that primes faster recovery; the present evidence does not settle whether it is mainly acclimation, selection, or another legacy effect."}],"decision":"answered","derivation_steps":[{"depends_on":[],"statement":"The stated evidence has two communities with the same measured species abundances immediately before the new heat pulse, but one had earlier heat pulses and the other did not; after the new pulse the previously exposed community recovers measured activity faster. Commitment: this reading would be contradicted if the problem described a different pre-pulse measured difference or a different recovery result.","step_index":1},{"depends_on":[1],"statement":"Because the measured species abundances are the same, the faster recovery cannot be attributed to a difference in those measured abundances at that time. Commitment: this would be contradicted by a demonstration that the measured abundances differed or that they alone predict the recovery difference.","step_index":2},{"depends_on":[1,2],"statement":"Therefore the earlier heat pulses must have left some persistent difference in community state that the reported measurements did not capture. Commitment: this would be contradicted if identical measured abundances plus the new pulse are sufficient to determine recovery and no unmeasured or hidden state differs.","step_index":3},{"depends_on":[3],"statement":"Candidate hidden differences include physiological acclimation such as heat-shock proteins, metabolic or dormancy states, strain-level selection or genetic change, extracellular factors, and other ecological memory. Commitment: each candidate is refutable by specific pre-pulse molecular, viability, strain-level, or transfer experiments that fail to show the predicted difference.","step_index":4},{"depends_on":[3,4],"statement":"The observed faster recovery is consistent with a priming or memory effect in which the previously exposed community is already closer to a stress-tolerant or active state and can resume measured activity sooner. Commitment: this would be contradicted if, after controlling for the hidden state, prior exposure no longer predicts faster recovery.","step_index":5},{"depends_on":[4,5],"statement":"The available evidence cannot uniquely identify which of these hidden mechanisms produced the difference. Commitment: this would be contradicted by an available measurement that already discriminates among acclimation, selection, and extracellular memory.","step_index":6},{"depends_on":[4,5,6],"statement":"The next investigation that would most help is a replicated, controlled time-series experiment standardizing both communities to the same measured species abundances and comparing them before, during, and after a heat pulse with strain-resolved and single-cell viability/activity assays plus transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, together with transplantation or conditioned-medium tests to determine whether the memory is carried by cells, extracellular factors, or selection. Commitment: this would be contradicted as the best next step if it cannot distinguish the leading mechanisms or if a simpler existing measurement already does so.","step_index":7}],"dispositions":[],"missing_derivation":""}
END WORKING ANSWER
